_contract: REGISTERED BEFORE ANY SESSION. Produces what the D2/D3 objective contract requires BEFORE D2's formal search: D3's lambda (lambda rule v2), the diagnostic thresholds (diagnostic_threshold_rule), the rollout-rescoring cost, and the D2 objective's overhead on the production state-evaluation and DEPTH paths. No D2 candidate exists when it runs and none is created. AUTHORIZES NOTHING: a session needs the maintainer's grant (authorization.json, absent until then).
question: on the standing incumbent B against the teacher, what are lambda and the registered diagnostic thresholds, and what does the D2 objective add to a state evaluation and to one DEPTH round on the production path?
order: after R0 (independent review, 2026-10-13: R0 first, then the reference calibration)
prediction_rows: the mode D2's search will run: all_v1, or scored_v1 if and only if R0's verdict is PASS and recorded before this session's authorization. The calibration pass is execution-independent (its own forwards); only the timing pairs read the mode
sequence: check-only preflight on the pod: B's identities and the $0 construction gate, the registered pool, the policy, both rule hashes
rebuild B from its one construction owner (A_bsz1, verified against all four identities), the GPU to itself
teacher and B forwards over the 147 unique items -> lambda and thresholds; rescoring timed on 24 items
WRITE reference_calibration.json and flush the partial record
state-evaluation pair (KL-only, D2, KL-only), only if the deadline covers 120 s
one DEPTH round at the root, KL-only then D2, each under a deliberately hoarded allocator pool, only if the deadline covers 645 s
never_records: the D2 objective's DEPTH choice or round table: only its timing. Nothing that looks like a D2 search result may exist before D2's search

acceptance.calibration: lambda_from_reference returns a value (it refuses a zero confidence IQR) and the pool is the registered 209 draws / 147 unique items
acceptance.timing: diagnostic: a skipped or failed pair is recorded and the cost model keeps its provisional factor for that path; it never invalidates the calibration
acceptance.raw_kl_control: reported (max |objective raw KL - KL-only teacher KL|); a large value is an engineering defect to diagnose
acceptance.cache_fix: diagnostic, recorded as timing_depth_one_round.cache_fix_validated: both arms entered the operator with < 1 GiB driver-free and > 1 GiB hoarded and still CACHED the reference -- the GPU evidence the allocator-hoard fix in _available_memory_bytes owes. False is a finding about the fix, not a failure of the session, and the D2 search keeps its recompute-mode price

hardware._peak_from: a3 stage D; stage P peaked at 16.29 GiB (a8). A 24 GB card is too tight

alternative.buys: both timing pairs even when every earlier component is at its maximum; a maintainer choice, not taken by this record

time_and_money._cap_vs_bill: the session cap sets the launcher's ssh window (cap / live rate); the watchdog stops the pod 12 min after it, so the worst bill exceeds the cap -- the grant covers that with the $0.30 teardown reserve inside it

command: ADOPT_CAMPAIGN=logs/stages/stage-1/families/d_series/validations/reference-calibration/v1/campaign.json ADOPT_COMMIT=<the commit that records the grant> ADOPT_BRANCH=exec/d1-behavioural-readiness ADOPT_STAGES=L ADOPT_PREDICTION_ROWS=<all_v1, or scored_v1 iff R0's recorded verdict is PASS> SESSION_CAP=1.18 nohup bash scripts/stages/stage-1/phase_d1/topk_adoption_launch.sh refcal_<utc> > artifacts/stages/stage-1/phase_d1/qualification/topk_adoption/refcal_<utc>.log 2>&1 &
